calendars.title: Calendars to mirror (blank = all)
calendars.description: Calendar names as Outlook shows them, such as Calendar or Birthdays

pastDays.title: Days of past events to mirror

futureDays.title: Days of upcoming events to mirror

clientSetup.appTypeNote: Register an app in Microsoft Entra (Azure portal) for any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts, and add the Mobile and desktop applications platform — a public client needs no client secret. Any loopback port works for the redirect. The same registration serves Outlook mail.
steps: Sign in at portal.azure.com and open Microsoft Entra ID, then App registrations, then New registration.
For supported account types choose 'Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts', so both work or school and Outlook.com sign-ins are accepted.
Under Authentication, add the 'Mobile and desktop applications' platform and enable the loopback redirect — any 127.0.0.1 port works.
No client secret is needed: this registration is a public client.
Under API permissions you may add the Microsoft Graph delegated permission Calendars.Read; otherwise you are asked to consent when you sign in.
Copy the Application (client) ID from the Overview page and paste it below.

notes: Works with Microsoft 365 work or school accounts and personal Outlook.com accounts; some organizations require an administrator to approve the app before you can sign in. Mirrors a sliding window: events from the last pastDays days (default 90) through the next futureDays days (default 365). Older events were never fetched, and an event that ages out of the window stays in the corpus rather than being pruned. The window moves forward about once a week. Recurring meetings are mirrored one record per occurrence. Deleted events, events rescheduled outside the window, and meetings their organizer cancelled are removed, even though Outlook keeps a cancelled meeting in your calendar until you delete it. Each calendar's folder is named cal- plus a short code derived from its ID, so it survives a rename; the calendar's name is in every record's calendar field. Every record uses the same fields as the Google Calendar connector.
